subject: Deployment defense matrix & next steps — isolation/airgap questions
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@dzonehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment defense matrix & next steps — isolation/airgap questions

Thanks again for the time this morning, Daniel — quick recap and concrete next steps to keep momentum.

Summary from our call:
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) for patient-facing inference workflows; HIPAA and GDPR applicability.
- Current compliance posture: you mentioned ISO 27001 in progress, SOC 2 timeline TBD, and an internal privacy review for GDPR data residency.
- Key technical asks from your security team: network isolation options, proof-of-concept for air-gapped ingestion, KMS/HSM support, and a short list of evidentiary artifacts for procurement.

Immediate asks / actions for DZone Health: (1) please upload your current network diagram (internal NAT, subnets, firewall placements) to the shared folder below, (2) complete the short vendor security questionnaire we attached, and (3) confirm whether you require HSM-backed key storage or customer-managed KMS.

What Redwood will deliver next:
- A two-page deployment defense matrix that maps: deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private) -> isolation controls -> evidence to satisfy procurement (SOC 2 artifacts, logs retention, network ACLs).
- A draft private deployment topology sketch tailored to the diagram you share.
- A proposed timeline and whom to include from our side (solutions engineer + security).

Proposed follow-up: 30–45 minute technical session on Tue/Wed next week with your security lead and our Solutions Engineer (Ben). Please suggest times.

Attachments: call-recording-20260816.mp3 (recording), vendor-questionnaire-link (Google Drive)

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cD_example-questionnaire

—
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0138
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@dzonehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: DZone Health Security Team <security@dzonehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 13:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment defense matrix & next steps — isolation/airgap questions

Thanks, Rishi — great summary. Looping in our security team for the technical session. Quick answers to your asks:

- SOC 2: not yet; we expect a SOC 2 Type I audit start in Q4 and Type II in Q2 next year. We can provide our ISO 27001 scope and current audit artifacts now.
- Network diagram: attaching a slightly redacted topology (dzone-prelim-arch.pdf). Our infra team runs in a VPC on Azure with private subnets, customer NATs, and strict egress policies.
- KMS/HSM: we use Azure Key Vault; for some PCI-adjacent workloads we can enable HSM. Will we need to store model keys there or just data encryption keys?
- Airgapped ingestion: we have an offline batch path for PHI ingestion that currently lands in an internal SFTP behind our DMZ. Can Redwood accept batched file pickup from an SFTP gateway or does it require physical media?

We uploaded the network diagram to the folder you linked. Also attaching a short architecture PDF for context.

Daniel Park
Head of Cloud Ops, DZone Health
daniel.park@dzonehealth.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@dzonehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment defense matrix & next steps — isolation/airgap questions

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the diagram — that helps a lot. Quick replies inline and a proposed agenda for the technical session.

Inline:
- SOC 2: good to know timeline; for procurement we can accept ISO artifacts + your roadmap to SOC 2 as interim evidence. We'll document what is acceptable in the defense matrix.
- Keys: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS integrations. For stronger security we can integrate with Azure Key Vault HSM-backed keys so model keys and data keys remain under your control. We should confirm the exact key types in the call.
- Airgapped ingestion: we support both SFTP pickup (scheduled, over a private peering tunnel) and an on-prem agent for environments that cannot have outbound connections. Physical media is also an option but operationally heavier.

Proposed tech call agenda (30–45m):
1) Review your uploaded topology (10m)
2) Discuss key management and HSM usage (10m)
3) Confirm egress/ingress controls and SFTP/on-prem agent options (10m)
4) Agree on evidence list for procurement and next milestones (5–15m)

Suggested attendees from Redwood: Ben Carter (Solutions Engineer) + myself. From DZone: your security lead + cloud ops.

Can we do Tue 08/18 at 10:00am PT or Wed 08/19 at 9:00am PT?

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (short explainer of what we can provide for RFI)

—
Rishi
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@dzonehealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment defense matrix & next steps — isolation/airgap questions

Thanks all — confirmed for Tue 08/18 10:00am PT. Two quick technical notes I want to cover in the call so we can be efficient:

- Egress filtering: if you enforce strict egress rules we typically recommend customer-managed NAT or proxy with allowlist to Redwood endpoints; we can also support an outbound-only, mutual-TLS-enabled peering connection for API traffic.
- Audit logs & evidence: we can provide token-level audit logs, per-route latency/cost breakdowns, and a package of SOC-relevant artifacts (controls mapping). If your procurement needs raw logs, tell us which retention window is required and we will confirm retention SLA.

If anyone on your side has a specific compliance checklist (HIPAA or a procurement RFI), please upload it to the Drive folder before the call so we can map answers against it live.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
